angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 738,833 km at 49.36 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: distance 49.364 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 49.364 +/- 0.642 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 20.1590 +/- 0.0285 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10), 708.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.062 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: radius 1.062 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.872 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.048) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 738,833 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5415 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: effective temperature 5415 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.078) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: effective temperature 5415 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.078) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 100777 (pscomppars): spectral type G8 V, from Philipot et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.107P/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 100777 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.27 dex, from Naef et al. 2007 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007A&A...470..721N/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 100777 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.02119, from Naef et al. 2007 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007A&A...470..721N/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 100777 (pscomppars): age 5.7 Gyr, from Philipot et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.107P/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 100777 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.8 km/s, from Philipot et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.107P/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.39 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 19 published values span log g 4.27 to 4.49, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
